endpoint.name: Twitter Tweet Transcript
endpoint.summary: Extract the spoken transcript from a Twitter/X video tweet by URL.

cost.note: 2 sources serve this, cheapest first; a failed attempt retries on the next, up to $0.036 at the dearest. The charge follows the answer's `costUsd`, not the listed price. Send X-Treg-Route-Max-Cost to refuse any source dearer than your ceiling. A not-found or empty answer is billed too, at its own `costUsd`.

url.note: Tweet URL of the video to transcribe (e.g. https://www.example.com/sample).

fields.note: Comma-separated keys (dotted paths descend) to keep on each result item. Trims the response, not the charge.

max_items.note: Caps the result rows returned; `_truncated` says how many were withheld. Not the charge.

summary.note: `true` returns only an outline: keys, item counts, per-field sizes.

jq.note: jq expression over the result envelope; its output replaces `output`. A failed expression returns the full result with `jqError`.

wallet.note: pay per call with a wallet, no account. A payment is at least $0.01; the call is charged only its real price, and the rest stays as this wallet's credit for its next calls (credit is not paid back as money).

samples.reason: Full transcript of a short native X video at the listed price.
Returned found:false, reason too_long for a 6 min 40 s native X video; no charge.
Result used to build the video's context for a how-to extraction.

provider.limits: no published per-key request-rate limit on /v1/run - AnyAPI does not advertise a quota it does not enforce. Spend is bounded instead by the wallet balance, the key's own spend cap, and the per-request `max_cost_usd` ceiling the caller sets. The unauthenticated /agent/signup trial route is limited to 3 per IP per hour.
